subject: E-Commerce
title: Winner-Take-Most Economics
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Winner-Take-Most Economics.

hook.text: In every region, 1-2 marketplaces capture 70%+ of online shopping. E-commerce is a winner-take-most industry.

buildup.text: Amazon dominates the US, Alibaba leads China, Mercado Libre owns Latin America, Shopee controls Southeast Asia.

discovery.text: Network effects, logistics infrastructure, and brand recognition compound advantages for the market leader.

twist.text: Second-place marketplaces survive but rarely thrive. Walmart.com has 6% of US e-commerce vs Amazon's 38%.

climax.text: Marketplace economics reward one dominant platform per region. Competition exists at the margins, not at the top.

punchline.text: 38% vs 6%. In marketplace wars, the winner takes most. The rest scramble.

quiz.question: What does 'winner-take-most' mean in marketplace economics?
options: 1-2 dominant platforms capture most of the market while others fight for the rest
